A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HRV research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete Appendices A–J are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original ordered-weakening analyses, image generation and editing experiments, multi-concept generation results, and human evaluations, including SDXL experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and human evaluations, including the quantitative results in Tables 1, 2, 6 and 12 and the extensive appendix examples.

M1.justification: HRV construction, concept strengthening and adjusting, and the P2P-HRV formulation remain unchanged. Section 5.3 and Appendix F clarify the existing A&E-HRV implementation, including noun-token selection and weighting before averaging, without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet/PromptHero construction prompts, core concepts, polysemy cases, five editing attributes and two multi-concept prompt types. The SDXL scenarios, Physical and Chemical Processes examples and Tableware extension were already present in v1.

E2.justification: Image editing retains SDEdit, P2P, PnP, MasaCtrl and FPE. Multi-concept comparisons retain Stable Diffusion, Structured Diffusion, A&E and the Appendix F.1 SynGen comparison. Table 6 also retains the same random-order controls; newly cited metric papers are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The reported prompt and image counts, metrics, 50 PNDM steps, guidance scale 7.5 and self-attention replacement rates remain unchanged. SD v1.4 was already specified in v1. The expanded random-order and BG-DINO descriptions disclose existing settings rather than revise the evaluation design.

E4.justification: The random-order comparison, rescaling-factor sensitivity, strengthening-versus-adjusting comparison, self-attention trade-off, timestep analysis and failure cases are retained. The new Section 4 reference to Appendix C.3 points to an analysis already reported in v1, with unchanged Table 6 results.

E5.justification: Seed counts remain unchanged: three in Appendix C.1, ten for the generation/editing evaluations and thirty for multi-concept generation. Table 4 retains its mean and standard-deviation reporting, and Table 6 retains three random-order cases. No new uncertainty estimates or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative examples are retained. Both versions report the misinterpretation reduction from 63.0% to 15.9%. Tables 2 and 12 retain A&E-HRV Type 2 scores of 0.3971, 0.2073 and 0.6580 for full-prompt similarity, minimum-object similarity and BLIP-score.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, Algorithm 1 and the HRV scaling arguments are unchanged. The added head indices in Section 3 and Figure 2 make notation consistent with the existing appendix formulation; they introduce no new mathematical definition, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract softens the polysemy claim from correction 'in most cases' to reducing misinterpretations. The introduction states cross-architecture usefulness more firmly, changing 'might' to 'can'. The central HRV, interpretability and three-task contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: Appendix E.3 adds a rationale for choosing DINOv2 based on its self-supervised representation. Appendix E.4 more explicitly explains the structure–alignment trade-off through increased dependence on source-image information. The existing failure conditions and SDXL normalization limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 specifies the random ordering and its reversal; E.3 explicitly identifies cosine similarity between segmented-image DINOv2 embeddings; F explains HRV weighting before attention averaging and noun-only application. Section 5.3 also corrects the A&E description from attention-map updates to latent updates using attention-derived gradients.

R1.justification: Appendix E.3 adds Kim et al. (2024) and Zhang et al. (2018), relating BG-DINO to prior region-based perceptual metrics. The abstract explicitly adopts mechanistic-interpretability framing. Consolidating the duplicate SDXL references does not remove a distinct prior work.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and selected explanatory paragraphs, refines terminology and headings, and adds acknowledgements and conference-header text. The overall section sequence and appendix organization remain stable; the editing is targeted rather than a substantial restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains explicit head-index notation, and captions including Figures 10, 21, 47 and 49 are refined. Conference headers and local text reflow alter some positioning. The existing figures and tables are retained without new experimental displays or a substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves technical precision by correcting the A&E update description and specifying the random control, BG-DINO computation and A&E-HRV integration more clearly (Section 5.3; Appendices C.3, E.3 and F). These details make the work easier to understand and reproduce. The gains are limited because the empirical evidence and documented limitations remain essentially unchanged.
